subject: humanities
passage: Long before movies existed, people could watch pictures move. One popular device of the 1800s was the zoetrope, a short drum with narrow slits cut around its side. A strip of drawings was placed inside the drum, each drawing showing a figure in a slightly different position. When the drum was spun and a viewer looked through the slits, the drawings seemed to blend into a single moving figure, such as a horse galloping or a juggler tossing balls.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: The zoetrope created the appearance of motion from a series of still drawings.
choices.B: Drawings of galloping horses were the most common subjects used in the zoetrope.
choices.C: Zoetropes were difficult to use because the viewer had to spin the drum by hand.
choices.D: The zoetrope was the most important invention leading to modern movies.

explanation.why: The text introduces the zoetrope as a device that let people "watch pictures move" before movies existed, and then explains how it worked: a strip of drawings, each slightly different, appeared to blend into a single moving figure when the drum was spun. The main idea is this effect of motion from still pictures.
explanation.A: Correct. The whole text explains how still drawings in a spinning drum appeared to move.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A galloping horse is given only as an example of a moving figure, not as the most common subject.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text never says the device was difficult to use.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text calls the zoetrope "one popular device" and never ranks it among inventions that led to movies.
